about.title: Susanville Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Susanville residents rely on a small number of local providers, and when one of those providers makes a preventable error, the ripple effects hit hard in a community this size. Medical malpractice covers more than obvious surgical mistakes — it includes missed diagnoses, medication errors, birth injuries, and failures to follow up on abnormal test results. California law places real hurdles in front of these claims: a short window to act, a mandatory 90-day notice before filing suit, and a requirement that a qualified medical expert review the case before it can move forward. Because Lassen County has limited hospital and specialist capacity, records and witnesses can be scattered across facilities, which makes early fact-gathering especially important. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney who can evaluate whether what happened to you falls outside the range of an acceptable bad outcome and into something legally actionable.

whyChoose.title: Why Susanville Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: You Won't Miss a Filing Deadline
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a malpractice claim. An attorney can help track that clock and the required 90-day pre-suit notice before it runs out.

items.title: Damage Caps Don't Mean No Case
items.desc: California's cap on non-economic damages rises each year under MICRA, but that cap doesn't apply to your medical bills or lost income. A knowledgeable attorney can explain how the current cap affects your specific claim.

items.title: Expert Review Comes Standard
items.desc: California almost always requires a qualified medical expert to support a malpractice claim before it can proceed. The independent attorneys in our network know how to line up that review so a bad outcome alone isn't mistaken for negligence — or overlooked when it is.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in Susanville?
items.answer: Under California law, you generally have one year from when you discover the injury, but never more than three years from the date it happened. There's also a 90-day notice requirement before a lawsuit can be filed, so it's worth talking to someone sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does a bad medical outcome automatically mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that not every complication or poor result is the result of negligence. An independent attorney, working with a qualified medical expert, looks at whether the provider's care fell below the accepted standard — not just whether the result was disappointing.

items.question: With limited providers in Lassen County, will my records be hard to gather?
items.answer: It can take extra coordination, since Susanville care often involves referrals to specialists outside the immediate area. An attorney connected through LawProactive can help track down the relevant records and identify who was involved in your care.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No, our connection service is free. Attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless your case results in a recovery.
